title: What is AI?
teaser: The big picture, from AI to generative AI

basics.say: Let's start at the very beginning. 'AI' is a big umbrella word – it covers any machine doing a task that usually needs human thinking.
Inside that umbrella sits machine learning. Instead of following hand-written rules, the machine learns patterns from lots of examples.
Think of a spam filter. Nobody lists every spam email. It sees thousands of examples and learns what spam tends to look like.
Deep learning is machine learning with many stacked layers – a 'neural network'. That's what made recognizing faces and voices possible.
And right in the middle: generative AI. It doesn't just recognize things – it creates new text, images or sound. That's what we'll explore here.

deeper.say: Here's the key difference. Traditional software: a person writes the rules. Machine learning: the machine finds the rules itself, from data.
A neural network is loosely inspired by the brain: millions of tiny adjustable numbers, called parameters, tuned during training.
Training is slow, expensive and happens once. Using the model afterwards – experts call it 'inference' – is fast. That's what happens when you chat.
One consequence: a model only knows what was in its training data, up to a cut-off date. Anything newer, it has to be told.

takeaway: Generative AI is the part of AI that creates new content – text, images, sound.
